smm_pool.title: Should You Optimize for a Custom Conversion?
smm_pool.text: When you choose the “maximize number of conversions” performance goal, you have to select a conversion event. This could be a standard event (like “purchase”), a custom event, or a custom conversion for the specific product that you’re selling in the ad. Using a custom conversion can make sense, and it’s not technically wrong. But I’d still recommend using the standard event in most cases. Here’s why… What is a Custom Conversion? First, let’s get this out of the way because it’s the source of common confusion. A custom conversion and a custom event are not the same thing. Standard Event: One of the predefined actions Meta has already named, such as Purchase, Lead, CompleteRegistration, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout, and ViewContent. Custom Event: A conversion event that is relevant to your business but cannot be defined with a standard event. I’ve created events like PodcastPlay, VideoPlay, and ScrollDepth that represent important actions and fall outside of the standard event definitions. Custom Conversion: Created without code, define a conversion using rules. Examples include creating a rule based on a specific URL or parameters sent with a standard or custom event. This allows you to isolate segments of a specific conversion type. For example, you can create custom conversions for all purchases over $50 or purchases of a specific blue shirt. Standard and custom events are usually created with code, though they don’t have to be. A purchase event is usually sent with the purchase of any product. A custom conversion can help focus on the purchase of a specific product. The Volume Problem In theory, optimizing for a custom conversion could help guide Meta toward the exact action you want, and it prevents inflated surface-level results . Because if you optimize for the purchase event, reported results don’t have to be for the product you’re promoting. Conversion volume is a common challenge for advertisers, especially when running sales campaigns. So if you’re already struggling to get conversion volume, optimizing for a custom conversion will limit volume even more. And volume is helpful for both you and Meta’s delivery optimization. If you’re getting very few conversions, Meta will assume your ads are failing. smm_pool.title: Meta Ads for Local Businesses
smm_pool.text: Local businesses present a special kind of challenge for Meta advertising. Your potential audience is limited, and you’re often focused on foot traffic instead of conversions. More often than not, budgets are also lower. While it’s a challenge, don’t overthink it. Performance Goal If you’re able to optimize for a purchase or lead, you’re at an advantage over many local businesses. Do that. While it’s not easy, by any means, you are at least better able to get Meta to prioritize the action you care about. If you can’t optimize for a conversion, you will probably need to optimize for a top-of-funnel action like reach, ad recall lift, ThruPlay views, or interactions. None of these are preferred, but our main goal is simply to show our ads and build some local brand awareness. Demographic Targeting Because we’re using this type of interaction as our performance goal, we have to be careful with demographic targeting . Since the delivery algorithm is literal , the biggest issues with waste happen because it’s not hard to find people to reach or get a basic reaction from. So if your ads go to an irrelevant demographic at a high rate ( confirm this first with breakdowns ), consider value rules to correct it by lowering bids . Always prioritize value rules over removing demographics entirely, unless you can’t legally serve a group. Location Targeting Then target people within a reasonable radius of your location. Though it’s a common strategy, resist the urge to remove people who live outside of that radius with exclusions . Since you can only target and exclude people who live or recently in a location, excluding people outside of a radius will also exclude people who live in your targeted area but travel outside of it. Because you’re targeting a local area, Meta will also automatically check a box to reach people who show interest in your area . Unless your business is a destination for outside tourists, you’ll want to uncheck it. Placements Whether you remove placements or use value rules here is up to you.
